title: Read the arrival date a guest typed

blocks.text: A hotel's booking form takes the arrival date as text, the way guests in Germany and the Netherlands write it: day, month and year separated by dots. Some guests pad with zeros and some don't:

Last spring the front desk found guests booked for nights they never asked for. A guest who mistyped the date should get "please check the arrival date" from the form, never a booking for some other day.
Finish `arrival(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/ArrivalDates.java`: the date the guest typed, or an empty `Optional` for text that names no date the calendar has. About six lines in total.

cases.says: a date typed with two-digit day and month is read, a leap day included
text in another form, an impossible month or an empty field gives no date
a day the month does not have gives no date instead of the month's last day
a day and month typed without a leading zero are read

origin.section: ofPattern Turns 30 February Into the 28th Unless the Resolver Is STRICT, and STRICT Needs uuuu

concepts: When parsing, dd demands two digits, while d also accepts a single digit.
A formatter from ofPattern resolves SMART and turns a day the month lacks into the month's last day; ResolverStyle.STRICT refuses it.
